summary: The None check in load_ssl_context_verify is inverted, so env-provided CA bundles are never used and default usage with trust_env and no env vars sets verify to None and crashes.

findings.explanation: The condition `if ca_bundle is None` is inverted. When SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR are set and valid, ca_bundle is not None so verify is never overridden and the feature does nothing. When no env var is set (the common case with trust_env=True and verify=True), self.verify is assigned None, so the following isinstance(self.verify, bool) fails and Path(None) raises TypeError, breaking all default HTTPS requests. The new test would also fail at its assertion that ssl_config.verify equals the env value.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `if ca_bundle is not None: self.verify = ca_bundle`.
